Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Components 7×7 board 1 on the centre square. 1 on the last played piece. 24 2×1 domino-shaped pieces: 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 Game play 2 players: More and Fewer . More starts. Each turn one piece is placed on the board, with the green counter on top. A piece may be placed anywhere it does not: overlap another piece, overlap the black counter, or touch an edge of a piece with the green counter. If a player does not have a legal move, they pass their turn and remove the green counter from the board. Game end Once no more moves can be made, the number of color groups on the board is counted. A color group is any set of one or more pieces of the same color that are connected vertically or horizontally. The Fewer player wins if the number of distinct groups of cells of the same color is fewer than 12 , otherwise the More player wins. Example 13 color groups ⇨ More player wins! This game is played on a 7x7 board with the center square blacked out. There are 24 pieces, 6 of 4 different colors. Each piece is a domino covering exactly two cells of the board. Both players choose pieces from a shared pool.

There are two players in the game: the starting player is called "More" and the other player is called "Fewer".

The goals of the game are opposite for both players. The "Fewer" player wins a finished game if the number of distinct groups of cells of the same color is less than 12. Otherwise the "More" player wins.

[Rating: 3.75/10] [i]Jugado en igGameCenter[/i]  Debo reconocerlo, me sentí un poco defraudado de este juego al descubrir que está "roto".  El juego tiene dos objetivos diferentes para los jugadores, y el jugador "More" tiene una ventaja (aproximada de 70-30) sobre el jugador "Fewer". En las partidas que he jugado, el juego es propenso a hacer 12 grupos. Un jugador debe tener cierto nivel de juego con respecto a su oponente para poder ganar con "Fewer", y no crean que es tan difícil de aprender la estrategia.  El juego en si es interesante como idea, pero precisa unos pequeños ajustes de juego para poder sacarl

[Rating: 5/10] I'm not sure why I wanted so badly to play this before I had-- maybe the non-partisan board combined with such qualitatively different goals? But now that I have played I also don't know what I think. Naive play left me confused. Reading strategy tips on the internet left me less confused but no more successful. There's got to be a game here, but how do I play it?

[Rating: 5/10] on BGA - 2 player abstract game with colors blocks. It was fine, nothing exciting but good to try. Basically harmless abstract.

[Rating: 5.5/10] An abstract game my wife will play. One player must make the most colored areas while the other makes the least. It's a very simple and quick thoughtful filler. I really enjoy playing this one. Another great Nestor game with perfect components and storage.

[Rating: 6/10] Worthwhile. The winning condition isn't as contrived as it sounded at first. There's quite a bit to think about; will come back to this.
